claims.text: Introducing a controlled density of SRO precipitates in tungsten or tungsten-based alloys will increase phonon scattering.
Increased phonon scattering from SRO precipitates will reduce the lattice component of thermal conductivity.
Tungsten has a robust, refractory lattice.
Tungsten is currently used or selected for plasma-facing components.
Tungsten provides a high-temperature, stable baseline in which the effect of SRO precipitates can be isolated and tuned.
Alloying additions, heat treatment, or irradiation can introduce or control SRO precipitates in tungsten-based materials.
Plasma-facing components operate under high-temperature conditions at or above approximately 1000 K.
The size, distribution, and density of SRO precipitates determine the relevant structural mediation of phonon scattering in the tungsten matrix.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
SRO precipitates reduce phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times diminish the ability of lattice vibrations to transport heat.
A tungsten matrix containing SRO precipitates will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than a homogeneous tungsten matrix.
Controlled SRO precipitates will produce a measurable decrease in lattice thermal conductivity relative to a precipitate-free tungsten baseline.
The magnitude of the expected decrease in lattice thermal conductivity is uncertain.
Pure tungsten has high thermal conductivity in plasma-facing applications.
Electronic heat conduction usually dominates over lattice heat conduction in metals.
The precipitate effect must be tested where the phonon contribution is significant or can be separated from electronic conduction.
Excessive precipitate formation or alternative irradiation-induced defects may complicate attribution of changes in thermal conductivity to SRO.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or a similar method can separate lattice and electronic contributions to tungsten's thermal conductivity under the proposed conditions.
TEM can quantify the density, size, and distribution of the proposed SRO precipitates.
